It is a web platform with two modes: automatic, where the models execute according to your settings, and manual, where you confirm each entry yourself. Entry costs US$250 and includes a demo.
We reviewed the public record: pricing, restrictions, support hours, payout wording and every claim in between. Where the record contradicts itself, the scorecard marks it down.
whatItClaims: A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
whatWeChecked: The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Submit your details and activate the account through the verification email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Fund US$250 via card or transfer to activate the trading balance.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your preferences, select automatic or manual execution, and run the practice account first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Risk settings before the first trade.
redFlags: Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.
A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.
Performance language with no dates attached.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
9 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

bottomLine: Zhundravise is a standard-issue AI trading desk with the usual strengths and the usual omissions. None of the omissions are dealbreakers - they are conditions.
Our 4.8 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
